Shop (Verkaufsraum) furnished in parts/room-1.mjs: two-run counter with cakes and candle cakes as the focal piece facing the door, bread rack on the west wall, bench by the west window, flour-barrel corner in the south-east, three hanging lanterns. Door approach (11,10), archway lane (11..12) and wing landing (15,2,15) are clear.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; room check says OK (walk 41 of 45 cells, the 4 unreached are the counter cells; light min 8, 0 dark). The room-1 part placed 29 blocks with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; the roof's off-palette polished_blackstone_brick_stairs is from roof.json, not this part.
left: plan.md has no room items in its checklist and elements.md's interior item covers all six rooms, so I left it unticked; only the shop is done.

In the rendered inside view a tall white block stands at the west end of the room. Probing the grid shows no white block in my cells, so it is probably a neighbouring part's wall or a render artefact; I did not confirm it.
Not placed: a wall shelf of flower pots or decorated pots and a rug carpet, which the brief mentions as optional dressing.

waste.what: Checking what a single cell holds by writing a one-off node script that imports the build library and loads build.nbt, to identify the white block seen in the render.
waste.cost: one script and one call, about 1 minute
waste.tool: `mcd info` or `mcd zoom --at x,y,z` on a cell, or a `mcd cell build.nbt x,y,z` query, would have given the block at a point without writing a script.

waste.what: Judging the interior by eye from the rendered room.png (the render shows an unidentified white block; the room check's floor grid shows furniture only as 'o').
waste.cost: one Read of the image plus one probe
waste.tool: `mcd room` floor grid could label each 'o' cell with its block id (e.g. 'b' bread rack, 'c' counter), so a designer would not need to probe the grid to read the furniture.
